features.name: Harness scaffolding
features.description: create-harness.mjs writes a complete harness into a target project: AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and init.sh at the project root, all state under harness/. Detects stack and package manager to build the verification commands, and skips existing files unless --force
features.evidence: Fresh scaffold on a node fixture scores 100/100; root holds exactly 3 harness files plus harness/. Re-running over an existing harness reports SKIPPED for every file and creates no duplicate.

features.name: Seven-subsystem scoring
features.description: validate-harness.mjs scores instructions, state, verification, scope, lifecycle, memory and behavioral as a percentage of 35, names the bottleneck, and exposes --json, --html, --budget, --log, --fail-fast, --no-fail and --min-score
features.evidence: 7 subsystems returned in --json output, 44 checks total (5+5+8+6+5+7+8). This repo scores 100/100; both bundled examples 100/100.

features.name: harness/ install layout with backward compatibility
features.description: Harness state lives under harness/, leaving three files at the project root. A harness on the older flat layout is still read, scored and repaired in place; detectHarnessLayout() prevents creating a split layout
features.evidence: Flat-layout harness scores 100/100, identical to the harness/ layout. Enriching a flat harness with progress.md deleted rewrote it flat and created no harness/ directory.

features.name: Gap enrichment of existing harnesses
features.description: enrich-harness.mjs identifies failing checks and applies canonical fixes: creating missing files from templates and splicing missing sections into the right place in files that already exist
features.evidence: Recreates a deleted progress.md on both layouts, then reports 'No gaps found'. Section insertion is markdown- and fence-aware, covered by scripts/insert-anchor.test.mjs (7 checks, run by ./init.sh).

features.name: Memory subsystem
features.description: A bounded always-on index, an append-only journal, and a graveyard of rejected routes each carrying an expiry condition. Two-step save invariant; link integrity checked in both directions so no lesson is dangling or orphaned
features.evidence: memory 5/5 on this repo and both examples. Index pointers resolve whether written sibling-relative, repo-root-relative or ./-prefixed — all three verified with 0 dangling, 0 orphaned.

features.name: Out-of-band curation (dreaming)
features.description: curate-memory.mjs reads the journal against the store and proposes lessons to harness/dream-queue.md. Counts the two countable signals, prints the three needing judgement, and never applies its own proposals
features.evidence: A token recurring across two dated journal entries produced one proposal in harness/dream-queue.md, with the human accept/reject gate present and nothing applied.

features.name: Environment contract
features.description: harness/environment.md declares external preconditions as table rows whose Check cell is a shell command. init.sh runs them first under their own heading and exits 1 with a machine-not-code message. Vacuously true when the file is absent
features.evidence: A passing requirement reports PASS and does not block; an unmet one exits 1. Verified against a real scaffold, since create-harness generates init.sh rather than copying the template.

features.name: Verification adversary (mutation gate)
features.description: mutate-gate.mjs breaks init.sh or the project in known ways and reports what went unnoticed, so a gate that verifies nothing is detectable. Wired into scoring via validate-harness.mjs --mutate
features.evidence: 3/3 mutants killed on this repo. Caught a real defect during development: a comment mentioning the fail-fast flag kept that check passing after the real line was removed.

features.name: Benchmark and HTML reporting
features.description: run-benchmark.mjs self-checks by scaffolding a throwaway harness, then scores the target and eval coverage. render-assessment-html.mjs renders a standalone report. Both write under harness/
features.evidence: Eval coverage 100/100 over 19 evals. harness/harness-benchmark.json and harness/harness-assessment.html both produced; --log appends to the resolved memory store.

features.name: This repo runs on its own harness
features.description: The repo eats its own output: AGENTS.md routed at harness/, a memory store, and an init.sh gate that verifies the things which can actually regress rather than echoing success
features.evidence: 83/100 before, 100/100 now with 3/3 mutants killed. ./init.sh syntax-checks all 8 scripts, runs the unit checks, and requires both examples to score 100 — probed to exit 1 on a broken script, a regressed example, and an unmet environment contract.

features.name: Close the two remaining known defects
features.description: Both examples' init.sh lacked the environment contract block, so neither demonstrated a feature the skill ships. templates/feature-list.schema.json carried YAML frontmatter and so was never parseable as the JSON Schema its extension promises. Found a third while fixing them: templates/init.sh named the fail-fast flag in a comment, which keeps that check green after the real line is deleted
features.evidence: Contract block inserted into both examples from initScriptFromCommands() output rather than transcribed, so it cannot drift from what create-harness generates. All three paths verified per example: passing requirement reports PASS, unmet exits 1, absent file does not block. Both still 100/100 and react-harness now kills 3/3 mutants. Schema metadata moved to a _meta key: valid JSON, and used to validate all four feature lists in the repo plus a negative control. Three new checks in index-coverage.test.mjs guard the class, each probed to fail.

features.name: Episodic session search
features.description: scripts/search-journal.mjs: parse dated journal blocks (reuse journalBlocks from curate-memory.mjs), score by keyword hits, print top blocks with dates and context. Options: <keywords> [--since DATE] [--count N]. Verification first: a .test.mjs fixture with two matching blocks (recency wins) written before the script; wired into init.sh and the eval suite. Closes the episodic-recall gap from docs/carbon_gap_memory.md (design decision in harness/open-work.md, P1).

features.name: Fold session-handoff.md into progress.md
features.description: session-handoff.md was a second home for state progress.md already carried (objective, blockers, files changed, decisions, next step), and the Required/Optional docs and the scorer had drifted around it twice. Remove the file from scaffolding, scoring and enrichment; progress.md gains a Recommended Next Step marker and now carries the end-of-session handoff alone
features.evidence: Fresh scaffold no longer creates session-handoff.md and scores 100/100 with the new progress.md. Enricher recreates a deleted progress.md including the Recommended Next Step section (probed on a copy of react-harness). Both bundled examples 100/100. New reverse assertion in index-coverage.test.mjs (listed Required but no longer enforced) regression-probed to catch a re-introduced session-handoff bullet, then passes clean. ./init.sh green; this repo 100/100, 3/3 mutants killed.

features.name: Scratchpad folder for rough work
features.description: Scaffold a scratchpad/ folder at the project root so an agent's throwaway scripts and intermediary code stay inside the repo — visible and reviewable — instead of scattering into temp dirs outside it. create-harness.mjs writes scratchpad/README.md; templates/agents.md adds a Working Rule routing rough work there; this repo gitignores scratchpad/
features.evidence: Fresh scaffold on a scratch target writes scratchpad/README.md alongside the other files. The Working Rule ('Rough work goes in scratchpad/') appears in templates/agents.md, the fresh target's AGENTS.md, and this repo's AGENTS.md. .gitignore lists scratchpad/. ./init.sh green; this repo 100/100, 3/3 mutants killed.

features.name: Output style artifact
features.description: Claude Code has a native output-style setting; most other agent runtimes do not. Add harness/style.md as an optional, auto-scaffolded template holding talk rules (tone, format, structure); templates/agents.md reads it at startup and follows it for every reply, so the behavior is portable to any agent that reads AGENTS.md, not just runtimes with native support. Optional and unscored, matching the dream-queue.md/graveyard.md pattern rather than the required set.
features.evidence: templates/style.md added with starter ELI5-style rules; templates/index.md lists it. create-harness.mjs writes it via copyTemplate alongside open-work.md. templates/agents.md startup step 2 reads it and the Optional Artifacts section documents it. Two new checks in index-coverage.test.mjs guard both wires (script writes it, agents.md mentions it). ./init.sh green; this repo's own 100/100 score and both bundled examples' 100/100 unaffected since the artifact is unscored.
